fields.name: job_name
fields.label: Job name
fields.help: Names the output directory for this run.

fields.name: sequence_molecules
fields.label: Molecules
fields.help: Add one box per unique protein, ligand, DNA, or RNA entity. Set its native Boltz chain ID (or comma-separated IDs for identical copies), sequence or ligand, cyclic flag, and residue modifications. A protein's MSA may be left blank (generated by the MSA server when it is on, otherwise single-sequence), set to an absolute .a3m or .csv path, or set to empty for single-sequence mode.

fields.name: constraints
fields.label: Constraints (JSON, optional)
fields.help: Native Boltz constraints array. Supports bond, pocket, and contact entries using the chain IDs above.

fields.name: templates
fields.label: Templates (JSON, optional)
fields.help: Native Boltz templates array. Each entry may select a CIF/PDB, chain mapping, force flag, and threshold.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties (JSON, optional)
fields.help: Native Boltz properties array, such as [{"affinity": {"binder": "B"}}].

fields.name: yaml_spec
fields.label: Boltz input (YAML)
fields.default:
version: 1
sequences:
  - protein:
      id: A
      sequence: QLEDSEVEAVAKGLEEMYANGVTEDNFKNYVKNNFAQQEIS
fields.help: Complete native Boltz YAML. Define protein, DNA, RNA, and ligand entities under sequences; optional constraints, templates, and affinity properties use the same schema as the Boltz CLI. A protein without an msa key gets one from the MSA server; give msa a path to supply your own, or msa: empty for single-sequence mode.
fields.help_note: Bio Web writes this text to input.yaml and passes that file to boltz predict.

fields.name: inputs_file
fields.label: Boltz input file (YAML)
fields.help: The YAML file defining this prediction, in the same schema as the Boltz CLI takes.
fields.help_note: Choose a file. Its contents are read here and sent as the input document.

fields.name: use_msa_server
fields.label: Use the public MSA server
fields.help: Generate an MSA for every protein that has no MSA of its own, using the ColabFold MMseqs2 server below. This sends those protein sequences to that server. Proteins with an MSA path or msa: empty are left as they are. Turn off for private sequences or offline runs; each protein then needs a path or msa: empty.

fields.name: msa_server_url
fields.label: MSA server URL
fields.help: ColabFold-compatible MMseqs2 endpoint; used only when the MSA server is on. The public server asks for serial queries from a single IP, so host your own for large batches.

fields.name: use_potentials
fields.label: Use inference-time potentials
fields.help: Apply Boltz-2 inference-time potentials to improve physical plausibility.

fields.name: recycling_steps
fields.label: Recycling steps
fields.help: Number of recycling steps. The Boltz CLI default is 3.

fields.name: sampling_steps
fields.label: Structure sampling steps
fields.help: Diffusion steps used for structure prediction. The Boltz CLI default is 200.

fields.name: diffusion_samples
fields.label: Structure samples
fields.help: Independent diffusion samples generated for each input.

fields.name: step_scale
fields.label: Structure step scale
fields.help: Diffusion temperature/step size. Boltz-2 defaults to 1.5 and recommends values between 1 and 2; lower values increase diversity.

fields.name: sampling_steps_affinity
fields.label: Affinity sampling steps
fields.help: Sampling steps for the affinity head. Used only when the YAML requests an affinity property.

fields.name: diffusion_samples_affinity
fields.label: Affinity samples
fields.help: Diffusion samples for the affinity head. The Boltz CLI default is 5.

fields.name: affinity_mw_correction
fields.label: Apply affinity molecular-weight correction
fields.help: Enable Boltz's molecular-weight correction for the affinity value head.

fields.name: seed
fields.label: Random seed
fields.help: Seed used by the Boltz random-number generator.
